_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. First print press 4.33.5 (run 20261015-074514-8f469b20); first release on press 4.34.2 (run 20261027-153346-829448e4). Credential-less: no vendor core; behaviour proven against a mock core built from Paessler's official API v2 OAS (tools/mock_prtg.py).

handfixes.summary: Generated sync has no sensors -> /sensors/{id}/data dependent
handfixes.why: The dependent makes one API call per sensor on every sync (cores commonly hold thousands of sensors, each request bounded by PRTG's 25 s execution timeout) to copy channel measurements no command reads from the mirror; 'sensors data <id>' still reads them live. With it present, a sync against an unreachable core also reported success. Re-apply: cli-factory/prtg/reprint-4342-20261027/tools/apply_handfixes.py.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: a per-dependent sync opt-out (x-pp-sync: false on the sub-collection) in the press

handfixes.summary: Root help reads 'PRTG Network Monitor CLI', not the slug-derived 'Prtg CLI'
handfixes.why: root.go.tmpl renders {{humanName .Name}} and ignores the spec's x-display-name (press 4.33.5 and 4.34.2).

handfixes.summary: No sync, export or store path reads GET /experimental/license; 'system license-info' reads live, without the response cache, and returns the whole body
handfixes.why: The license body carries the PRTG license key. Press 4.33.5 made it the 'system' sync/export resource (the generic store used the key as the row id, FTS-indexed); press 4.34.2 maps 'system' to /experimental/featureflags instead, and the asserts fail if a later press moves it back. The generated 'auto' read writes the body through to the local store and caches it on disk.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: a per-endpoint x-pp-syncable: false / no-cache extension in the press

asserts.contains: resolveReadWithStrategyAndResponsePath(cmd.Context(), c, flags, "live", "system", false, path, params, nil, "", cmd.ErrOrStderr())

handfixes.summary: Every API request and redirect hop goes only to the scheme, host and port the configuration resolved when the client was built (for --core, the registered core's server); anything else is refused before it is resolved, dialled or given the key
handfixes.why: Work order host pinning. The generated client sends the Bearer key to whatever URL a request names; a Location header, sync --path-context or an MCP argument could move one client's key to another host. originPinTripper (hand file internal/cli/prtg_guard.go, applied to every CLI, fleet-child and MCP client from applyPRTGTransport after the TLS setting) compares a byte-exact ASCII-folded origin (a host with any non-ASCII byte never matches) and the same check runs FIRST in CheckRedirect, before the generated redirect guard. Tests: TestOriginPinRefusesRedirectToAnotherHost, TestNormalizedOriginRefusesNonASCIIAndFillsPorts.

asserts.contains: c.HTTPClient.Transport = originPinTripper{origin: origin, next: responseHoldTripper{next: next}}

handfixes.summary: The on-disk HTTP response cache is off for every API client
handfixes.why: PRTG bodies carry the license key and credential settings (windowsloginpassword, snmp communities, ...), and an echoed key would land in cache files. c.NoCache = true in guardClient (prtg_guard.go), every client. Proven by the black-box file scan (prove_bb.sh no-cache).

handfixes.summary: Every store write passes mergeIncomingResourceData, which redacts credential-named fields (the one rule fleet output uses); a statement carrying a held credential is refused by the kit's SQL driver (credkit-sqlite-every-handle).
handfixes.why: Sync, the write-through cache and the keep-richer merge all store raw API bodies; PRTG include sections carry Windows/Linux/ESX/SNMP credential settings and an echoing core could repeat the key. mergeIncomingResourceData returns withoutStoredSecrets(...) (hand file internal/store/prtg_secrets.go; rule cliutil.SecretFieldName in prtg_secrets.go, shared with fleet.Redact). Numbers, booleans and null are kept (counts such as total_tokens). Codex review r1 [P1]: an id repeating the key reached resources.id and resources_fts.id (the id is resolved before the strip); resourceStorageID and upsertGenericResourceTx now pass storedID. Proven by the black-box file scan (prove_bb.sh store-strip, store-id).

asserts.contains: func SecretField(name string) bool { return cliutil.SecretFieldName(name) }

handfixes.summary: Every credential a request body or a response carries is held before the request is sent or any command reads the body: credential-named JSON strings at any depth (request values of 4+ characters, response values of 8+ that are not PRTG's **** masks), the response decoded per Content-Encoding exactly as the client decodes it
handfixes.why: Work order: minted tokens join the holder before anything can print. Codex review r1 [P1]: a deflate-encoded CreateAPIKeyResponse.key reached stdout (the POST-only hold parsed the body before the client decompressed it); the license key (LicenseInfo.key) printed in license-info output and its --deliver file; a password sent in a --stdin body was echoed back unheld. Class fix: responseHoldTripper (hand file internal/cli/prtg_guard.go) holds request-body and response credential fields for every method; ReadBody/DecodeBody (hand file internal/client/prtg_decode.go) reuse the client's own size cap and decoder. Behaviour change: session login, users api-keys create and system license-info print the notice in place of the token, key or license key. Tests: TestResponseCredentialsHeld; the black-box battery (license-info JSON/CSV/table/--deliver, deflate api-keys create, session login --stdin).

asserts.contains: c.HTTPClient.Transport = originPinTripper{origin: origin, next: responseHoldTripper{next: next}}

handfixes.summary: the press spec (library spec.yaml, not shipped in this repo) declares x-pp-mutation on every operation that is not a GET (true; false only for the lookup POST /users/api-keys/find), so prtg_execute previews every state-changing call until confirm and prtg_read refuses it
handfixes.why: Codex review r1 [P1] write without confirm: the press reads a POST whose body is only a PRTG filter as a search, so /sensors|devices|groups|probes/resume and /scan and /users/pause|resume ran from MCP prtg_read without confirm, even with PRTG_MCP_READ_ONLY=1. Spec-encoded by tools/derive_spec.py step 7, so it survives every reprint by construction; the test catches a press that stops honouring it. msp-skills does not ship the spec, so the ledger asserts its generated effect: at least 61 code_orch endpoints need confirm (every non-GET but the lookup).

handfixes.summary: The MCP context tool reports archetype infrastructure and carries no chat-API insights
handfixes.why: The profiler scores channels (communication) and probe_network (infrastructure) +2 each and breaks the tie in Go map order, so a render emits archetype communication with 'Message search' / 'Channel health' insights at random (seen at 4.33.5 and 4.34.2). Re-apply: tools/apply_handfixes.py fix_mcp_archetype.

handfixes.summary: Mirrored MCP tools that can change PRTG state (fleet ack, fleet pause, fleet resume, import, any later non-read-only command) preview and send only with confirm: true; the fleet actions preview with the CLI's own per-core preview and send by the gate adding --yes
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.2 gates prtg_execute on confirm, but the Cobra-tree mirror registers fleet_ack/fleet_pause/fleet_resume (which could only ever preview: --yes is a blocked tool argument) and import with no confirm. RequireConfirmForMirroredWrites (hand file internal/mcp/cobratree/prtg_confirm.go), called from RegisterTools right after RegisterAll, wraps every mirrored tool that is not read-only, not mcp:local-write and not sync/export/fleet sync/workflow archive, so a command added later is gated by default. Only boolean true sends; confirm is never forwarded; --yes stays a blocked argument and is added only by the gate for commands annotated prtg:sends-with-yes. Mock e2e: previews 0 POSTs, confirm true sends. Tests: TestRegisteredMirroredWritesNeedConfirm (fails without the tools.go line), TestSendsWithYesPreviewsThenSendsWithYes, TestMirroredWriteNeedsBooleanConfirm.

asserts.contains: if confirmed, ok := args["confirm"].(bool); ok && confirmed {

handfixes.summary: A bulk action reports success only when every item succeeded: one shared reader of PRTG ActionResult lists (fleet.ActionOutcomes / ResponseFailure) fails the whole result on any failure signal from any item, with per-item detail, in the generated multi-* commands, the fleet action engine and MCP prtg_execute
handfixes.why: Codex review r2 [P1] failed bulk action reported successful: sensors multi-resume with PRTG's documented '200: Success with one failure' body printed success:true and exited 0 (the generated detectPartialFailure only knows partialFailureError). Orchestrator order: any failure signal from any item (a failure member that is not null whatever it holds, a populated error field, success:false, an HTTP status of 400+ or failure wording in a status field, an entry naming no node) makes the whole result a failure. detectPartialFailure calls prtgActionFailure first (one line in helpers.go; --allow-partial-failure still downgrades); the fleet engine's actionResults uses the same reader; the API transport reports any write response with a failed item to the MCP call's record (cliutil.ReportActionFailure) and the MCP middleware fails that call. Tests: TestBulkActionPerItemFailureFailsTheCommand, TestFleetActionResultsAnyFailureSignalWins, TestBulkActionFailureFailsCLIAndMCP (built binaries); prove_c.sh.

handfixes.summary: fleet handoff reports every sensor that is up now, switched to up inside the window and has a recorded last_down at or before that switch as recovered, whatever interrupted the way back (pause and resume, acknowledgement, rescheduled interval), with via=direct or via=after_gap; CLI and MCP fleet_handoff both expose it
handfixes.why: Codex review r1/r2 [P1] omitted recovery events: the window and scanning-interval rules dropped real recoveries (down at the 15:00 hourly scan, up at 16:00; interval changed before recovery). Orchestrator order: whatever handoff the run interrupts (pause, acknowledge, resume) has a recovery path that the CLI and MCP both expose and test. Hand file (survives a reprint); recorded for the tests. Tests: TestHandoffNeverOmitsAnInterruptedRecovery, TestHandoffRecoveryOnCLIAndMCP (built binaries), e2e (mock core).

handfixes.summary: Every registered core's API key comes from ONE variable, PRTG_FLEET_KEYS (name=key entries separated by commas and/or newlines; fleet.ParseKeys), read only by its literal name in internal/fleet/keys.go. Core.KeyEnv, core add --key-env and every os.Getenv/EnvOverride of a computed name are gone; a legacy fleet.json key_env field is ignored. A child pinned to core C gets PRTG_FLEET_KEYS=C=<key> only (fleet.Scrub drops the inherited value with every other PRTG_* variable, case-insensitively); --core narrows its own process the same way. HoldCredentials holds the raw value and every parsed key, and on a parse failure every fragment, before any output. Parse errors name the entry position, never key text.
handfixes.why: check_env_schema.py cannot resolve an operator-named credential variable and has no waiver for one; one literal PRTG_FLEET_KEYS keeps every credential read visible and declarable on all three install channels, and keys stay off disk.

handfixes.summary: users multi-pause-request, sensors multi-acknowledge and ai analyze-aiincidents carry no "create" alias.
handfixes.why: The press assigns alias "create" to every POST, so `users create` paused every matching user account and `sensors create` acknowledged every matching alarm: a bulk state change behind the most innocent verb (verify_all row 'no destructive create alias'). Commands that really create (devices create-sensor, groups create-device-for, groups create-for, probes create-*) keep theirs.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real argument-free GET with the real credential and refuses to dial the shipped https://{server}/api/v2 template, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and printing 'present, not verified'
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every guide tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works. The 4.34.2 print called any response to GET / reachable and never probed the credential, so an expired API key and a base_url aimed at the PRTG web UI both read as healthy, and the placeholder state never named PRTG_BASE_URL. doctor_verdict.go is the fleet helper (grafted from the acronis 4.34.0 copy, the same templated-base shape); replay_handfixes.py's doctor-verdict recipe wires doctor.go. Gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: --allow-partial-failure changes only the exit code; a generated action whose result has a failed item always reports success: false
handfixes.why: The press computes the mutation envelope's success as (partialFailure == nil || flags.allowPartialFailure), so `sensors multi-resume --allow-partial-failure --json` against PRTG's documented 200 response with a failed item (spec /sensors/resume 200 example 'Success with one failure') reported success: true and exit 0 with every item failed (Codex r1). Every generated mutation command now computes success from the outcome alone. Test: TestBulkActionFailureFailsCLIAndMCP.

handfixes.summary: no redirect is followed, same origin included
handfixes.why: The origin pin refused off-origin redirects, but a same-origin 302 was followed and the generated redirect hook re-attached Authorization (Codex r1: GET /version -> 302 /capture). The PRTG v2 API answers its own paths directly, so guardClient refuses every redirect. Test: TestOriginPinRefusesSameOriginRedirect.

handfixes.summary: GET /session (renews the session) previews until confirm over MCP, is refused under PRTG_MCP_READ_ONLY, and is refused by fleet exec and the raw child
handfixes.why: The spec documents GET /session as 'Renews an active user session.', a state change, but the read classifier keys on the verb, so prtg_read ran it under PRTG_MCP_READ_ONLY (Codex r1). One list (cliutil.StateChangingGET) feeds the MCP confirm resolution, the session.renew endpoint flags, the CLI annotation and cleanAPIPath. The factory spec derivation should set x-pp-mutation: true on GET /session so a reprint generates it. Tests: TestStateChangingGETNeedsConfirm, TestCleanAPIPathRefusesStateChangingGET.

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand and replaces this connector's own funnel, chokepoint and SQLite wrapper. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal; each main starts with credkit.Start and ends with credkit.Exit; the API client and feedback client go through credkit.Transport under the origin pin; every file write except the 0600 credential store and config file goes through the kit (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile is that declared exemption); stdout and stderr are the kit's pipes.
handfixes.why: One contract, one matcher and one set of sinks replace the connector-only copies, and a matcher fix reaches this connector by vendoring.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring (Declarations from the auth spec, Start and Exit in each main, kit sinks in the file, HTTP, SQL and MCP templates).

handfixes.summary: Every SQLite handle goes through credkit.SQLDriver: internal/credsql registers the one driver and every sql.Open in store.go and platform/migration.go names it, the read-only opener included. The MCP sql value cap moved from sqlite.Limit on a held connection to a DSN parameter.
handfixes.why: A statement's text and bound values are a sink of their own, reads included.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate store, migration and MCP sql opens against one kit-wrapped driver name.

handfixes.summary: credkit.MCPHTTP writes every response the MCP HTTP server serves, refusals included. requireBearerAuthWithLimits runs a preflight that writes nothing, then credkit.MCPHTTP around a gate that answers the Origin, bearer and body-limit verdicts.
handfixes.why: With the kit wrapping only the inner handler, a refusal answers outside it, and a token holding the word unauthorized would get a piece of itself back.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the MCP HTTP auth wrapper so its refusals are written by the kit-wrapped handler.

handfixes.summary: The config is held before it is parsed, by a line scanner that survives a malformed file, and parse errors name the file and line and never quote a value.
handfixes.why: go-toml's errors quote the file's text, so a credential in a malformed config could print, and a quoted value withheld the whole message so the operator lost the file name.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the kit's config loader template.

handfixes.summary: A credential from disk is only sent to the core its file names: refuseFileCredentialsElsewhere clears file keys and headers when PRTG_SERVER or PRTG_BASE_URL point elsewhere, and a saved credential stays bound to its origin.
handfixes.why: With a saved key, PRTG_SERVER=<other core> would otherwise hand one client's key to another client's core.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: bind file credentials to the origin they were saved for.

handfixes.summary: A --stdin body is held before a generated command parses it, every member of a duplicate key included.
handfixes.why: Generated commands parse --stdin into a map, losing every member of a duplicate key but the last. The kit also holds the whole body from StdinFlags, which covers a body that does not parse.

handfixes.summary: PRTG_CORE selects the core for the MCP server's native tools as well as its mirrored ones, keeps the server's own controls (read-only, no-local-data, HTTP bearer), and a selection naming no core stops the server.
handfixes.why: The MCP server has no root command, so the selector never ran for its native tools, and the selection's scrub dropped the operator's switches.

handfixes.summary: config.toml keeps only the server of template_vars, and no path context can set the server.
handfixes.why: The sync path-context argument was merged into TemplateVars: server=<host> moved the origin pin and the key with it, and the token save wrote it to config.toml.

handfixes.summary: A saved profile's value under a credential flag's name or base-url is held at startup, every duplicate included, in the config directory, the legacy path, under --home and under a registered core's home.
handfixes.why: Profiles replay their values as flags, so a profile is a credential file the rest of the program never reads as one.

handfixes.summary: a row the credential kit withholds from the store is skipped and named; the rest of the batch is stored and sync keeps walking, then ends that resource failed with the row ids
handfixes.why: One withheld row aborted the whole batch transaction, and sync returned on it, so a single large ordinary record (or one that really carried a held credential) stopped the resource and every row after it was never synced (#612, hubspot-calls-crm). The row is still withheld; it is now named in a sync_error event and in the resource's error, the run exits non-zero, and the watermark stays so the next run fetches it again. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe withheld-rows).

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.
